audit.why: 47.86% over 117 games, identical in both sources. A losing but close lane matches the kits: Lillia's Blooming Blows stacks move speed on every ability hit while Sejuani's only gap-close is an 18-second charge, so the spacing game is hers until Glacial Prison exists. Left alone.

Lillia for levels 1 through 5 then Skill from 6 onward, and the captions agree — the flip is Glacial Prison arriving at 1300 range against a champion whose whole defence is spacing. Nothing needed re-siding, and both win-rate sources agree here so there was no reason to doubt the shape.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors and one large omission. early says 'her Lilting Lullaby DOT ticks through shield health' — Lilting Lullaby is her ultimate, a sleep; the damage-over-time is Dream-Laden Bough, her passive. mid says Glacial Prison's 'blizzard zone roots anyone caught inside'; Riot's text says the bola 'freezes and stuns the first champion hit and creates an ice storm that slows other enemies' — a slow, not a root. late recommends Warmog's or Heartsteel on the grounds that 'her AP DOT won't meaningfully penetrate two tank items'. And nowhere does the page state the condition on her ultimate: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.'
audit.why: The item advice is backwards and it is the costliest error here. Dream-Laden Bough deals 'additional max Health damage over time', so stacking Warmog's and Heartsteel makes her passive hit harder, not softer — the page recommends the exact build that feeds her. The ultimate condition is the free win the page never mentions: Lilting Lullaby only touches enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so if Lillia has not landed a skill on Sejuani, her ultimate does nothing to Sejuani at all. That turns 'respect her R' into a concrete rule — break contact after her passive expires and the sleep cannot reach you. The root-versus-slow error matters because a Sejuani who believes her own blizzard roots will commit to a chase it does not support.
audit.corrected: Dream-Laden Bough named correctly in early and wants.foe[1]; the blizzard corrected to a slow in mid and whys[4]; the max-health scaling and its item consequence rewritten in late; the Dream Dust condition on her ultimate stated in wants.foe[2], spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and that is accurate — not a single number appears in any field.
audit.why: The numbers are what make this lane playable. Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds and is her only slow; Watch Out! Eep! is 14 seconds at rank 1 and is the circle the page tells you to avoid standing in; Blooming Blows is 6 seconds and is what builds her speed stacks; Lilting Lullaby is 150 seconds at rank 1. Telling a Sejuani to punish 'when she steps up' without any of these is advice she cannot act on.
audit.corrected: Swirlseed's 12s, Watch Out! Eep!'s 14s, Blooming Blows' 6s and the ultimate's 150s now appear in whys[1], whys[3], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit details never reach the page: Blooming Blows deals true damage on its outer edge, and Swirlseed is a slow that Frost Armor ignores.
audit.why: Riot's Blooming Blows text: 'deal magic damage to nearby enemies, dealing extra true damage on the edge.' The edge is the dangerous part, so the counterintuitive rule against a 450-range Q is that standing closer to her is safer than standing at its rim — worth knowing for a champion whose plan is to be in melee anyway. And Fury of the North grants 'immunity to slows', so Swirlseed's slow — Lillia's only one — does nothing to a Sejuani with Frost Armor up, which is the single biggest hole in her kiting pattern.
audit.corrected: The edge true damage is in whys[1]; the slow immunity against Swirlseed is in early and wants.you[0].

edits.after: Swirlseed and Watch Out! Eep! land before your Q closes, and Blooming Blows adds true damage on its outer edge — her rim hurts more than her centre.

edits.before: At Level 1 this is a passive CS contest — neither of you has meaningful kill threat, but Lillia's Blooming Blows passive lets her walk away from any auto you throw. Farm with W and accept the poke; your Permafrost armor only activates when you haven't been hit recently, so tanking her DOT immediately strips your passive. At Level 2 you get Arctic Assault, but she can simply bounce out of your knockup range with the kite speed she's already building — don't burn Q forward unless she's trapped against terrain. Level 3 is your first combo window: Q into the second strike of Winter's Wrath stacks Frost, then Permafrost stuns her, but she can abort it by moving perpendicular the moment your Q animation starts. Take Doran's Shield and Second Wind; her Lilting Lullaby DOT ticks through shield health and the sustain is the only way you hold HP equity here.
edits.after: At Level 1 this is a passive CS contest — neither of you has kill threat, but Blooming Blows lets her walk away from any auto you throw. Farm with W and accept the poke; Frost Armor only rebuilds when you have not been hit recently, so eating her passive burn immediately strips your resistances. One thing works in your favour from the start: Swirlseed is her only slow, and Fury of the North makes you immune to slows while Frost Armor holds, so it does not stop your walk-up. At Level 2 you get Arctic Assault, but she bounces out of knockup range on stacked speed — do not burn Q forward unless she is trapped against terrain. Level 3 is your first combo window: Q into the second strike of Winter's Wrath stacks Frost and Permafrost stuns her, though she can abort it by moving perpendicular as your Q starts. Take Doran's Shield and Second Wind; Dream-Laden Bough ticks regardless and sustain is your only HP equity.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are rough — she can keep her W circle on your feet every time you try to Frost-trade, the DOT stacks deny your passive resistances, and she can E-bounce away the instant Permafrost comes out. Don't waste cooldowns chasing a Lillia who already has three Blooming Blows speed stacks; you'll overextend and die to her jungler. At Level 6 your dynamic changes sharply: Glacial Prison is a long-range CC that travels faster than she can react, and the blizzard zone roots anyone caught inside, including her. If you hit the comet she can no longer kite freely, and W-E finishes the stun chain. Use R to punish her whenever she steps up to DOT the wave.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are rough — Watch Out! Eep! is 14 seconds at rank 1 and she will put it on your feet every time you Frost-trade, while Dream-Laden Bough's burn keeps your Frost Armor from rebuilding. Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds and is her only slow, which Frost Armor ignores, so the thing that actually kites you is Blooming Blows speed, not the seed. Do not chase a Lillia who already has stacks. At Level 6 the dynamic changes: Glacial Prison stuns the first champion it hits and drops an ice storm that slows everyone else, which is enough to end her spacing. Remember her ultimate only sleeps enemies already carrying Dream Dust — stay clean and its 150 seconds are wasted.

edits.before: In full teamfights Sejuani is the bigger threat — your Glacial Prison into E-stun CC chain locks multiple targets and chains directly into Lillia's own Lilting Lullaby sleep, meaning you hard-enable her ult even while being her counter. Run Sunfire Aegis into Warmog's or Heartsteel; her AP DOT won't meaningfully penetrate two tank items. Never duel her in the open without your R up: she will kite your whole kit, land Watch Out! Eep! on your head, and run away at full health while your passive resistances are stripped. Win by being the tank that sticks to her carries and forces her to fight in a confined teamfight rather than a free-kite open field.
edits.after: In teamfights Sejuani is the bigger threat — Glacial Prison into a Permafrost chain locks multiple targets and sets up Lilting Lullaby, so you enable her ultimate even while countering her. Do not build Warmog's or Heartsteel into her: Dream-Laden Bough deals damage as a share of your max health, so raw HP stacking makes her passive hit harder rather than softer. Take Sunfire Aegis into magic resist instead, and buy it before her first item rather than after. Never duel her in the open without R up; she will kite your whole kit, land Watch Out! Eep! on your head, and leave at full health. Win by sticking to her carries and forcing a confined fight rather than a free-kite open field.

notes: Both win-rate sources agree exactly here (47.86, 117 games). The most consequential fix is in late: the page recommended Warmog's or Heartsteel on the reasoning that her damage-over-time cannot penetrate tank items, but Dream-Laden Bough deals additional max-health damage, so those two items specifically increase what she does to you. That advice was actively harmful and is now reversed toward Sunfire plus magic resist. The 'Permafrost armor' and 'Permafrost resistances' mislabel for Fury of the North survives in whys[2] and spikes[2], which I had no separate reason to open. Not asserted: whether being woken from Lilting Lullaby's sleep by Sejuani's own Winter's Wrath wastes the bonus damage on a minion-tick versus a champion hit, and whether tenacity shortens the Drowsy phase — neither is answerable from lillia.json, whose needsResearch is empty.
